run_metadata.coverage_summary: SEVERELY DEGRADED RUN. The execution environment enforced a global outbound-egress block: WebFetch failed DNS resolution for every host and direct HTTPS (curl) returned 403 CONNECT-rejected for all destinations including google.com, so NO tender portal or detail page could be opened. The only working external channel was WebSearch (routed via Anthropic infrastructure), which returns titles/URLs and model-summarised snippets but cannot query live portals, follow pagination, or open detail/specification documents. Tier 1 (AusTender, buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, Tenders ACT/WA/SA, QTenders, NT QTOL), Tier 2 (VendorPanel, councils, GBEs) and Tier 3 (SAP Ariba/Business Network Discovery, BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside, Woolworths/Coles) were all attempted via WebSearch only. Five currently-open opportunities previously captured (when WebFetch worked) were independently re-corroborated as still open via WebSearch and are carried forward at headline level; no new deliverables detail could be extracted. Five new buyer-originated local-government sources were identified.
gaps: CRITICAL TOOLING OUTAGE: WebFetch returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every host (including en.wikipedia.org); curl via the agent proxy returned 403 connect_rejected for every destination tested including www.google.com, www.tenders.gov.au and www.tenders.nsw.gov.au. Outbound egress is blocked for this session, so no live tender portal, detail page or specification document could be opened. Only WebSearch was available.

Because detail pages were unreachable, NO deliverables/requirements/evaluation/document extraction was possible this run. All 5 tenders are headline-level only and counted in entries_pending_detail; their headline fields were re-confirmed from WebSearch snippets of buyer-originated portals and must be re-verified on the live portals.

Tier 1 live portals (AusTender, buy.nsw, tenders.vic, tenders.act, tenders.wa, tenders.sa, QTenders/supply.qld, NT QTOL) could not be crawled; only cached search snippets were visible. Exhaustive Tier 1 coverage was NOT achieved this run.

WA: an official tenders.wa.gov.au snippet showed only a maintenance/closure notice; specific WA opportunities (e.g. Dept of Justice waste-disposal tenders, Gold Corporation geotechnical assessments) appeared ONLY via third-party aggregators (australiantenders.com.au, govmarket.com.au, govscanner.com.au) and could not be confirmed on the buyer portal, so they were NOT recorded as tenders (aggregator data is a discovery signal only).

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Business Network Discovery (formerly SAP Ariba Discovery, service.ariba.com/Discovery.aw) and major-buyer portals (BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Woodside, Woolworths, Coles) are registration/login-gated and were not reachable; no publicly-visible corporate RFx could be confirmed. No corporate opportunities were invented. These portals remain recorded in prior discovered_sources.
Invitation-only corporate RFx (e.g. management-consultancy RFPs) remain out of scope and were not fabricated.

De-duplication: the 5 carried-forward tenders reuse their existing dedup_keys; the aggregate retains their original first_seen (2026-10-16..2026-10-20) via min-date folding even though first_seen is set to the run date in this file.
